questions.question: When should you choose an architecture style, per FSA’s flow?
options: Before you know any characteristics or logical components at all.
After analyzing characteristics and logical components the system needs.
Only after rewriting the UI three times in different frameworks.
Never — styles are banned in modern engineering culture in real production systems at scale.
questions.explanation: Once an architect has analyzed the architectural characteristics and logical components… they know enough to choose an appropriate architecture style

reference.excerpt: Once an architect has analyzed the architectural characteristics and logical components… they know enough to choose an appropriate architecture style

questions.question: Why would microservices have been “inconceivably expensive” in 2002?
options: Because open source databases did not exist as an idea yet in any form in real production systems at scale.
Commercial licenses for OS, app servers, and DBs per service made isolation costly.
Because DNS could not resolve more than one hostname per company in real production systems at scale.
Because load balancers were illegal for commercial websites then in real production systems at scale.
questions.explanation: trying to build an architecture like microservices would have been inconceivably expensive

reference.excerpt: trying to build an architecture like microservices would have been inconceivably expensive

questions.question: A modular monolith is often a good early choice because:
options: It maximizes network hops and operational complexity from day one in real production systems at scale.
It keeps deploy simple while still allowing clear internal module boundaries.
It forbids any database and forces all state into browser cookies only.
It guarantees infinite scale without ever adding caches or replicas in real production systems at scale.
questions.explanation: Choosing an architectural style involves finding the easiest implementation path

reference.excerpt: Choosing an architectural style involves finding the easiest implementation path

questions.question: Making the web tier stateless supports:
options: Pinning every user forever to one specific web server process only.
Horizontal scaling of web servers behind a load balancer.
Deleting the load balancer because sticky sessions become mandatory.
Storing all sessions only in local disk folders on each web box.

reference.book: System Design Interview – An Insider's Guide

questions.question: Structural decay happens when:
options: Developers’ changes undermine required architectural characteristics over time.
You document every decision in an ADR and review fitness functions in real production systems at scale.
Load stays flat and characteristics are continuously verified in CI in real production systems at scale.
Architects continually analyze vitality of older architectures in real production systems at scale.
questions.explanation: structural decay, which occurs when developers make coding or design changes that impact the required architectural characteristics
